text:
sasha: heads up — zodiac15b int4 canary is showing a perf + quality delta after yesterday's quant rollout. p50 went from ~85ms -> ~120ms on our perf rig, p95 up ~2.2x. also seeing a handful of low-prob hallucinations on long summaries.

matt: ugh. did the canary traffic shape match the benchmark? could be different prompt distro.

sasha: yes we replayed the same eval set. throughput down ~18% for same batch settings (microbatch=8, batch_window=12ms). memory churn went up too — fragmentation metric spiked on the hosts.

ana: can you paste the perf numbers and a sample low-quality output? also which quant config (per-channel, symmetric?)

sasha: numbers: baseline fp16 p50=85ms p95=190ms. int4 canary p50=120ms p95=420ms. tail latency variance higher. sample QA fail: "asserts wrong year for source" on long context >6k tokens. quant config: 4-bit asymmetric per-tensor with our default fold/eight steps.

kevin: fragmentation suggests allocator churn. Any large allocations during decode? max_new_tokens setting for this test?

sasha: max_new_tokens=1024 (default). We saw a few requests that hit 800-1000 tokens. spikes correlate with the larger ones.

jess: 1024 seems risky for int4; our slot compaction and KV prefetch behave differently under quantized kernels. Could push default to 256 for this model until we stabilize.

matt: agree. immediate mitigations: 1) lower model default max_new_tokens to 256 2) set batch_window from 12ms -> 8ms to reduce coalescing pressure 3) enable soft-kv-evict trim at 80% to keep fragmentation down

ana: can we repro OOM locally with a few long requests? I'll run a stress script that sends mixed 200/800 token prompts.

sasha: running now on canary node group, attaching small trace:

```
2026-03-22T14:02:12Z decode: alloc peak 12.6GB
2026-03-22T14:02:12Z kv_prefetch triggered for session_id=9f3a..
2026-03-22T14:02:13Z slab_free_list thrash: +1200 ops
2026-03-22T14:02:13Z p95 latency jump
```

kevin: slab_free_list thrash + kv_prefetch is classic frag. Two fixes we used before: reserve a small warmup cushion (1.5GB) on canary hosts and tune prefetch to only prefetch embedded KV page ranges for >512 tokens.

jess: +1 on warmup cushion. Also consider temporarily switching quant backend to int8 for the high-latency tail experiments so we can isolate whether int4 kernels cause kernel scheduling issues.

matt: good call. Plan: A) rollback quant to int8 for 10% of canary traffic B) lower max_new_tokens default to 256 for zodiac15b C) adjust batch_window to 8ms and soft-evict trim threshold D) add warmup cushion on 3 canary nodes E) run eval suite for quality regression and perf for 24h

sasha: will implement A/B/C now. kicking rollout job -- @ci-bot can you create a canary patch with those flags?

ci-bot: created patch canary/1745678901-quant-mitigation, 3 nodes, 10% traffic. Deploy in progress :rocket:

ana: I'll run the QA eval harness against both int4 and int8 variants once patch is live and share diff report (precision@k, rouge, and hallucination rate).

kevin: after we have the eval diffs, we can decide whether int4 needs a different quant recipe (per-channel + outlier clamp) or just defaults tuned. also long-term we should add a `max_new_tokens_sensible_default` in model metadata so each model ships with safer defaults.

jess: logging a follow-up ticket for metadata defaults and a playbook entry for int4 rollouts — tagging @platform for slot reservation automation.

matt: thanks team. Sasha — ping when the 24h run finishes and paste the eval diffs. If tails improve, we can slowly ramp.

sasha: will do. early note: after soft-evict and lowering batch_window, p50 down to ~95ms and p95 to ~210ms on first 2-hour pass. quality diffs pending.

jess: :thumbsup:

sasha: closing loop — will post full artifacts in the rollout thread once CI finishes and QA runs complete.
